message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit but drivers must drive at a safe speed for conditions. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers and drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians always have the right‑of‑way at crosswalks. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Stopping distance: 20 ft on two‑lane roads, 30 ft on multi‑lane roads. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is only allowed on multi‑lane roads with a left‑hand lane for passing. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 15 ft of a stop sign, crosswalk, or fire hydrant.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked otherwise. | | **Toll Roads** | • Texas has both toll and free interstate segments.
• Toll payments can be made via TxTag, E‑Tag, or cash at toll plazas. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection; some counties also require emissions testing. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are used on many interstates and major roads.
• Violations result in fines and points on the driver’s record. | | **Points System & License Suspension** | • Accumulating 4 or more points in 12 months can lead to license suspension.
• Points are added for violations such as speeding, DUI, reckless driving, etc. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles must wear helmets.
• Commercial vehicles must follow specific weight, size, and licensing requirements. | ### Where to Find Official Texts - **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Provides driver handbooks, updated regulations, and enforcement notices. - **Texas Legislature Online** – For legislative history and amendments. ### Quick Tips for Compliance 1. **Always obey posted signs and signals.** 2. **Keep your vehicle’s registration and inspection stickers up to date.** 3. **Use hands‑free devices if you need to talk on the phone.** 4. **Check local ordinances**—some cities have stricter parking or speed limits than state law. If you need more detailed information on a specific rule or want to check the latest updates, let me know!
